openings.claim: Preserve insertion stops and adjustable elastic clamps, but disconnect their simultaneous load-bearing interface: swing each stop clear only after its rod is clamped. The clamp alone then maintains the registered position.
openings.delta: Tentatively use four trimmed plywood pieces as two orthogonal datum seats and the remaining two as captive pivoting stop leaves. Bolts join seats, pivot leaves and anchor adjustable elastic loops; cord retains loose hardware. Keep the entire joint within 90 mm. Each stop still supplies a fixed insertion contact while closed. After clamping, retract both leaves without compensating rod adjustments. Comparator uses the same assembly with leaves remaining engaged.
openings.prediction: If stop contact competing with clamp seating causes exchange error, retracted leaves should reduce return displacement, especially on the 18 mm substitution, without increased loaded displacement. Nearest rival: clamp friction/compliance or operator seating causes the error; retracting stops then provides no repeatability advantage or worsens drift. These are speculative mechanisms, not explanations established by the two supplied trials.
openings.probe: Within fabrication time, establish captive hardware, insertion contacts, clearance and envelope; abandon if these cannot coexist. Test two configurations with twelve exchanges each: five of each original rod followed by two 18 mm exchanges replacing the smaller rod. Alternate configuration blocks, restore the marked setup before each block, and record elapsed exchange time and pointer return displacement. Give each configuration four ten-second 10 N load trials spanning both rod sizes; record displacement during loading. Include retraction time in exchanges. Do not reseat after retraction. Twelve exchanges do not establish the full original-rod endurance outcome under every load.
assumptions: Available bolt lengths permit captive assembly and suitable loop anchors.
Elastic loops provide adjustable closing force against datums without rod modification; capacity is unknown.
Stop retraction clears rods without disturbing their clamped positions.
Defeat: return advantage absent, any target/load/time failure, hardware escape, envelope excess, or fabrication/testing budget exceeded. All constraints remain binding.

assessment: One bounded interface-break candidate. Retraction removes stop load support while retaining its insertion function. Feasibility and elastic restraint remain unknown; this comparator probe authorizes no deployment or promised performance.
